analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027 (Macro Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains) [Presentation]
key_insights: GS frames the market as a maturing cycle. The slide titles cover valuation drag, tech diversification, bonds regaining hedging value, a more cyclical dollar, rising value of gold and real assets, and EM resilience. The text extract carries titles and chart labels only, with no stated forecasts or return targets.

Global equities tend to do well when earnings growth is good, but the second derivative (change in the growth rate) matters. The chart compares 12m equity vs 10y bond returns against equity carry (dividend yield plus ex-post 12m EPS growth) relative to the US 10y yield, from 1950.

Valuation drag has already been material. The slide says global equity valuations have de-rated materially, indicating markets are pricing an earnings growth slowdown. The chart plots the 1-year change in NTM P/E against 12m-ahead NTM EPS growth.

Bond-like equities can help diversify tech. As in the Tech Bubble, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has increased (chart of 3-month beta on daily returns and 1-year beta on weekly returns).
Bonds reclaim macro and hedging value. The slide title says bonds have regained their macro and hedging role. Correlations are based on ES and TY futures. No correlation levels are given in the text.

Oil sensitivity is a driver of bond performance. One chart plots 10y bond total returns since January 1, 2026 against 2y1y sensitivity to oil prices, under the Europe & UK section titled 'Global Shocks and Local Shifts'.
The dollar is described as 'A More Cyclical Dollar' and Asian currencies as 'Revaluing'. The extract gives no levels or forecasts for either.

Equity has historically outperformed credit, especially during tech booms. The chart shows relative excess return of equity vs credit, with credit excess return scaled to match equity volatility and equity excess return measured vs T-bills.

Over the last 5 years, allocations to gold and other real assets have materially improved performance vs standard 60/40 portfolios. The chart shows the 5-year rolling Sharpe ratio for 60% S&P 500/40% US 10-year bonds, 60/40 with gold, and 60/40 with a real asset index, from 1950.
Energy is framed as 'Balancing Risk and Risk Premium'. The chart text says grey lines represent historical performance between 2011 and 2024. No price views are given.
EM is framed as 'Resilience and Diversification' across two slides, with no numeric content in the extracted text.
earnings_insights: Global equities tend to do well with good earnings growth, but the second derivative of growth matters. The chart uses equity carry defined as dividend yield plus ex-post 12m EPS growth, with a consensus-EPS-based variant.
Markets are pricing an earnings growth slowdown, as indicated by the material de-rating in global NTM P/E.

trade_ideas.description: Add gold and other real assets to a standard 60/40 portfolio, in place of part of the bond allocation.
trade_ideas.rationale: Over the last 5 years, allocations to gold and other real assets have materially improved performance vs standard 60/40 portfolios (5-year rolling Sharpe ratio).

trade_ideas.description: Hold bond-like (negative-beta) equities to diversify tech exposure.
trade_ideas.rationale: The proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has increased, as in the Tech Bubble, so bond-like equities can help diversify tech.

risk_factors: Second-derivative risk: a slowdown in the rate of earnings growth can hurt equities even when earnings growth stays positive.
Tech concentration, with bond-like equities offered as the diversifier.
Oil-price sensitivity of 2y1y rates, which affects 10y bond returns, especially in Europe and the UK.

Chart: 1-year change in NTM P/E vs 12m-ahead growth in NTM EPS, 1990 to 2025.
Chart: proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta, 3-month beta on daily returns and 1-year beta on weekly returns, 1990 to 2025.
Chart: 10y bond total returns since January 1, 2026 vs 2y1y sensitivity to oil prices.
Chart: 5-year rolling Sharpe ratio for 60% S&P 500/40% US 10-year bonds, 60% S&P 500/40% gold and 60% S&P 500/40% real asset index, 1950 to 2025.
vol_and_positioning: The proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has increased, as it did during the Tech Bubble. The slide pitches bond-like equities as a diversifier for tech exposure.
